flagged.evidence: The item cites Durrett, 5th ed., Section 2.2 for the uniform-integrability/L1 equivalence. In the current cited PDF, Section 2.2 is “Weak Laws of Large Numbers”; the relevant equivalence is Theorem 4.6.3 (p. 252), which states under probability convergence that uniform integrability and L1 convergence are equivalent. Thus the stated locator does not support this claim.

The item attributes d_0([X],[Y])=E[min(1,|X-Y|)] to Durrett Exercise 3.2.8. The current exercise instead defines beta(X,Y)=E[|X-Y|/(1+|X-Y|)] and compares beta with the Ky Fan metric. This is a different formula, so the cited statement does not license the displayed d_0 definition.

The example assumes only “a_k\downarrow0”, while step 1.1 invokes convergence in probability at threshold a_k, which requires a_k>0. On a one-point probability space take X_n=1/n, X=0, a_k=0, and b_k=2^{-k-2}. All written assumptions hold, but P(|X_{n_k}-X|>a_k)=1 is never <b_k, for any subsequence.
